title: A commission sheet that updates itself

docs.syntax: =sales*VLOOKUP(sales,tiers,2,TRUE) reads the rate the sales figure has reached
docs.explain:
The fourth argument of VLOOKUP decides how it matches. With TRUE, it walks down column A, stops at the largest tier floor the sales figure has reached, and returns the rate beside it. Sales of 4200 reach the 4000 floor, so the rate comes back at five per cent.

In C2 that rate multiplies the sales figure, so Ana's commission is 210. The second screen asks for the rate alone, 0.05, so the lookup and the multiplication come apart into two steps. Keep the rate in the table: 0.05 typed into a formula works today and breaks the next time finance moves a tier.

The table has to stay sorted by tier floor, lowest first, because TRUE reads down the column and stops at the last floor it passes. An unsorted table returns a rate from the wrong band and shows no error. Lock the reference as $A$7:$B$9 so the formula fills down the commission column without drifting.

errors.text: The fourth argument is FALSE, so VLOOKUP looks for a row equal to 4200 and finds none.
The column number points past the second column of the rate table.
The tier floors are out of order, so TRUE stops at the wrong floor and reads the wrong rate.

seo.title: Commission tiers with approximate VLOOKUP
seo.description: TRUE in the fourth argument stops at the largest tier the sales figure has reached, so 4200 pays the 4000 rate and a moved tier needs no edit.
